violations.description: Hardcoded AWS access key ID and secret access key literals are embedded directly in Terraform configuration files.
violations.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials from Terraform files and inject them securely via environment variables or secret management services.

violations.description: Hardcoded AWS access key ID and secret access key literals are embedded directly in Terraform lambda configuration.
violations.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials from Terraform files and inject them securely via environment variables or secret management services.

violations.description: Hardcoded AWS credentials export statements embedded in EC2 user data shell script.
violations.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials from EC2 user data and use IAM instance profiles or secure secret injection.

violations.description: The repository contains no test suite or test files to validate code functionality or security assertions.
violations.evidence: No test directory or test files exist in the repository tree.
violations.recommendation: Implement automated unit and integration tests for the project.

violations.description: GitHub Actions workflows use mutable action references (@main, @master) instead of immutable full-length commit hashes or pinned version tags.
violations.recommendation: Pin GitHub Actions to immutable commit SHAs (e.g. @v1.2.3 or commit hash).

violations.description: Python requirements file contains an extremely old and vulnerable dependency version without a modern lockfile structure.
violations.recommendation: Update dependencies to secure versions and use a robust dependency management tool with a lockfile.
